resources.string: Replaces the cover art on the car screen with live visualization while playing. Read the legal notice before enabling.
Rules about screens visible to the driver in your country

This option displays constantly moving graphics (oscilloscope, chips activity) on the car screen. In many countries it is illegal for a screen in the driver\'s field of view to show content that is not related to driving or navigation while the vehicle is moving, and such content is a dangerous distraction.

France: article R412-6-2 of the Code de la route prohibits placing in the field of view of the driver of a moving vehicle an operating device with a screen that is not a driving or navigation aid. It is a 5th class offence with the loss of 3 licence points and possible confiscation of the device.

Germany: § 23 (1a) StVO allows the driver to look at electronic devices, screens included, only briefly and as adapted to the traffic situation. Watching moving pictures while driving is subject to a fine and penalty points.

United Kingdom: regulation 109 of the Road Vehicles (Construction and Use) Regulations 1986 prohibits driving while a screen showing anything other than vehicle, road, navigation or driver assistance information is visible to the driver.

United States: many states prohibit operating a vehicle while a video screen showing entertainment is visible to the driver (for example California Vehicle Code § 27602). Distracted driving laws apply in every state.
Europe: national road codes require the driver to keep full attention on the road and most of them restrict screens showing content unrelated to driving that are visible to the driver.
Road rules about screens and distraction differ between countries and regions. Check the regulations where you drive.

This notice is general information, not legal advice. You remain solely responsible for using this option in compliance with local law: keep it for passengers or for when the vehicle is parked. Android Auto may also ignore or slow down the updates.
